world.title: Gulf crude exports near pre-war levels despite Hormuz attacks
world.summary: Non-Iranian crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returned to roughly pre-war levels in the final week of September, averaging 13.5 million barrels a day from Sept. 22 to 28, according to Kpler. Separately, Kpler data showed that at least 16.5 million barrels a day left the wider region in September, excluding I
world.content: Non-Iranian crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz returned to roughly pre-war levels in the final week of September, averaging 13.5 million barrels a day from Sept. 22 to 28, according to Kpler. Separately, Kpler data showed that at least 16.5 million barrels a day left the wider region in September, excluding Iran, matching its pre-war average. Producers and shipping companies have used pipeline routes and ship-to-ship transfers, while U.S. forces escort some vessels. Tanker attacks continue, shortages of refined fuel persist and diesel prices have risen despite stronger crude flows. The European Union reported record diesel pump prices on Oct. 1, while prices also rose in the United States. A U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports has disrupted Iran’s own seaborne oil exports.
world.image_alt: Gulf crude exports near pre-war levels despite Hormuz attacks

world.title: Premier League finds Manchester City guilty of nearly all 115 charges
world.summary: The Premier League said Tuesday that Manchester City was guilty of almost all 115 charges involving financial rules for the 2009-10 to 2017-18 seasons. The independent commission found that the Abu Dhabi-owned club used “sham” arrangements to inflate revenue and conceal funding; news reports put the sums involved above
world.content: The Premier League said Tuesday that Manchester City was guilty of almost all 115 charges involving financial rules for the 2009-10 to 2017-18 seasons. The independent commission found that the Abu Dhabi-owned club used “sham” arrangements to inflate revenue and conceal funding; news reports put the sums involved above £900 million. City denies wrongdoing and says it will appeal. The case became public in February 2023, when the league detailed 80 alleged breaches. The commission also found City guilty of most charges related to its failure to cooperate with the investigation. Sanctions have not yet been announced. Possible penalties include points deductions or expulsion from the Premier League. City’s appeal is due by Friday, Oct. 2, 2026.
world.image_alt: Premier League finds Manchester City guilty of nearly all 115 charges

world.title: U.S. sends 9,000 troops and third carrier toward Iran
world.summary: The United States is sending about 9,000 troops aboard ships to the Middle East, including the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt and an amphibious group carrying roughly 2,000 Marines, as President Donald Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran. The deployment would add to two U.S. carriers already in the region, th
world.content: The United States is sending about 9,000 troops aboard ships to the Middle East, including the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt and an amphibious group carrying roughly 2,000 Marines, as President Donald Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran. The deployment would add to two U.S. carriers already in the region, though officials have given differing arrival estimates: as early as the end of October in one account, or by the end of November in others. Trump has said escalation after the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections remains possible. He also said early indications linked Iran to a FlyDubai co-pilot accused of stabbing the captain and trying to crash an Israel-bound flight. He offered no details and said the matter was still under investigation. Trump warned that the United States would retaliate if a connection were established. Fighting is entering its eighth month, and diplomatic contacts are under discussion. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran had not avoided dialogue with Washington, but said it had been attacked three times during negotiations.
world.image_alt: U.S. sends 9,000 troops and third carrier toward Iran

world.title: South Korea threatens Ukraine with measures over disclosure of North Korean POW transfer
world.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified measures against Ukraine on Oct. 2 unless Kyiv acknowledges a confidentiality arrangement covering the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war and publicly apologizes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed the transfer in his Sept. 23 address
world.content: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified measures against Ukraine on Oct. 2 unless Kyiv acknowledges a confidentiality arrangement covering the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war and publicly apologizes. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy disclosed the transfer in his Sept. 23 address to the U.N. General Assembly, triggering a dispute between Seoul and Kyiv. Seoul says Ukraine had agreed to keep the transfer confidential to protect the soldiers and their relatives from possible North Korean retaliation. Ukrainian officials deny that such an agreement existed. Lee said Kyiv’s denial made him appear to be a liar and called the issue a matter of national dignity. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha has called the dispute a “diplomatic misunderstanding” and said Kyiv is working to resolve it. The South Korean and Ukrainian foreign ministers are discussing the tone, content and timing of Ukraine’s response, a senior South Korean official said on Oct. 2.
world.image_alt: South Korea threatens Ukraine with measures over disclosure of North Korean POW transfer

world.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever ties as Tigray fighting escalates
world.summary: Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara on Thursday, Oct. 1, and ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave within 48 hours, accusing them of activities that threatened national security. Eritrea responded by severing all diplomatic ties, saying Addis Ababa’s actions left it no choice. The diplomatic break followed renewed f
world.content: Ethiopia closed its embassy in Asmara on Thursday, Oct. 1, and ordered 10 Eritrean diplomats to leave within 48 hours, accusing them of activities that threatened national security. Eritrea responded by severing all diplomatic ties, saying Addis Ababa’s actions left it no choice. The diplomatic break followed renewed fighting in northern Ethiopia. Federal forces have been battling an opposition alliance led by the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Ethiopia has accused Eritrea, Sudan and Egypt of supporting the alliance; all three countries deny the allegation. Explosions were heard overnight in Addis Ababa, including near the military headquarters. Ethiopia and Eritrea restored relations in 2018 and fought alongside each other in Ethiopia’s 2020-2022 war. That war ended with the Pretoria peace agreement, though key provisions remained unimplemented. Ethiopia gave the expelled diplomats 48 hours to leave.
world.image_alt: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever ties as Tigray fighting escalates

world.title: Putin warns Russia may use nuclear arsenal if Kaliningrad attacked
world.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin warned on Oct. 1 that Russia could use any weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear arms, if Kaliningrad or other Russian territory came under direct attack. Speaking at the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow, he said Russia did not plan to attack European countries and presented the war
world.content: Russian President Vladimir Putin warned on Oct. 1 that Russia could use any weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear arms, if Kaliningrad or other Russian territory came under direct attack. Speaking at the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow, he said Russia did not plan to attack European countries and presented the warning as a response to what he called Western escalation. Putin cited NATO military exercises in the Baltic Sea, attempts to detain Russian vessels and Western discussion of possible future conflict with Moscow. NATO describes its exercises as defensive; Russia has accused the alliance of preparing to isolate Kaliningrad, the Russian exclave between Poland and Lithuania. Moscow had warned NATO in late September that an air or sea blockade of Kaliningrad could prompt retaliation, including the use of nuclear weapons. Putin reiterated that warning. NATO members and Russia are also trading accusations over military activity and hybrid attacks.
world.image_alt: Putin warns Russia may use nuclear arsenal if Kaliningrad attacked

world.title: SpaceX Crew-13 docks at ISS after record-fast U.S. flight
world.summary: SpaceX’s Crew-13 reached the International Space Station on Oct. 1, docking 7 hours and 55 minutes after a Falcon 9 launch from Florida. The transit set a record for the fastest trip to the station by a U.S. spacecraft. The four-person crew consists of NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canadian astronau
world.content: SpaceX’s Crew-13 reached the International Space Station on Oct. 1, docking 7 hours and 55 minutes after a Falcon 9 launch from Florida. The transit set a record for the fastest trip to the station by a U.S. spacecraft. The four-person crew consists of NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canadian astronaut Joshua Kutryk and Russian cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov. Watkins became the first Black woman to command a crew to orbit. The crew is scheduled to spend about six months aboard the station conducting research and maintenance, including studies of human health and performance intended to inform future missions to the Moon and Mars. The launch was delayed about three weeks after a leak was found in the Dragon capsule’s propulsion system, requiring a valve replacement. Crew-13 is taking over from four astronauts who have been aboard since February. Their return to Earth was expected as early as Monday, Oct. 5, weather permitting.
world.image_alt: SpaceX Crew-13 docks at ISS after record-fast U.S. flight

world.title: French student protests spread nationwide, forcing more than 400 schools to close
world.summary: Protests by French high-school students over staffing, crowded classrooms and deteriorating facilities spread nationwide, prompting Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu to convene a crisis cabinet meeting on Thursday, Oct. 1, and cancel ministers’ travel. Education Minister Édouard Geffray said more than 400 schools and ot
world.content: Protests by French high-school students over staffing, crowded classrooms and deteriorating facilities spread nationwide, prompting Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu to convene a crisis cabinet meeting on Thursday, Oct. 1, and cancel ministers’ travel. Education Minister Édouard Geffray said more than 400 schools and other education sites would remain closed Friday, with many shifting to remote lessons. Police made 1,949 arrests on Thursday, and the Interior Ministry said 305 police officers and gendarmes were injured. Nearly 3,000 students had been detained since the protests began, the Guardian reported. Fires were reported at schools in Nantes and Rouen, and university students joined demonstrations that blocked campuses in several cities. The government faces opposition to proposed 2027 budget cuts, and campaigning has begun ahead of next May’s presidential election, when President Emmanuel Macron cannot seek another consecutive term. Geffray was due to meet student representatives on Friday.
world.image_alt: French student protests spread nationwide, forcing more than 400 schools to close

business.title: Bank of England chief warns AI bets could trigger market shocks
business.summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned that heavy investment in artificial intelligence could trigger financial-market shocks if expected returns fail to materialize, saying the central bank is watching the money flowing to AI companies “very carefully”. Asked whether an AI bubble could burst, he said a correcti
business.content: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey warned that heavy investment in artificial intelligence could trigger financial-market shocks if expected returns fail to materialize, saying the central bank is watching the money flowing to AI companies “very carefully”. Asked whether an AI bubble could burst, he said a correction in asset prices was possible but did not predict when. Bailey said AI could strengthen economic growth but also carries substantial risks. Investors have valued Nvidia at $5.5 trillion, while Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon are spending hundreds of billions of dollars on the technology. Bailey said the Bank of England was prepared to respond to market shocks and would work to ensure the financial system remained resilient.
business.image_alt: Bank of England chief warns AI bets could trigger market shocks

business.title: Google limits Gemini 4 Argon launch to vetted cybersecurity partners
business.summary: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon on Sept. 30 but restricted access to vetted cybersecurity partners, saying hackers could misuse the model’s capabilities. The company is also giving the U.S. government early access through a voluntary pre-release safety process and has not set a date for public availability. The launch f
business.content: Google unveiled Gemini 4 Argon on Sept. 30 but restricted access to vetted cybersecurity partners, saying hackers could misuse the model’s capabilities. The company is also giving the U.S. government early access through a voluntary pre-release safety process and has not set a date for public availability. The launch follows months of delays as Google seeks to compete with OpenAI and Anthropic. Google said Argon outperformed rival models on some company-reported benchmarks, but it lagged on two of the four coding tests the company disclosed. Google had planned to release Gemini 3.5 Pro in June but did not do so.
business.image_alt: Google limits Gemini 4 Argon launch to vetted cybersecurity partners

business.title: Authentic Brands Group explores $6 billion takeover of Mattel
business.summary: Authentic Brands Group has approached Mattel and is discussing a possible offer above $20 a share, which would value the Barbie maker at about $6 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported. Mattel shares rose 18.8% on Thursday after the report. Mattel is preparing for a change in chief executive: Roger Lynch, currently
business.content: Authentic Brands Group has approached Mattel and is discussing a possible offer above $20 a share, which would value the Barbie maker at about $6 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported. Mattel shares rose 18.8% on Thursday after the report. Mattel is preparing for a change in chief executive: Roger Lynch, currently Condé Nast’s chief executive, is due to take over in November, replacing Ynon Kreiz, who is leaving for Paramount. Mattel’s market value was about $3.8 billion after the share rise. It is unclear whether the company will engage with Authentic’s approach; another bidder could emerge, and Lynch’s strategy as incoming chief executive may affect a deal.
business.image_alt: Authentic Brands Group explores $6 billion takeover of Mattel

business.title: U.S. sends carrier strike group and 9,000 troops toward Middle East
business.summary: The U.S. military has sent the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and an amphibious readiness group toward the Middle East with roughly 9,000 personnel as President Donald Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran. The ships are expected to reach the region by the end of November; some accounts put the deployment a
business.content: The U.S. military has sent the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and an amphibious readiness group toward the Middle East with roughly 9,000 personnel as President Donald Trump weighs renewed strikes on Iran. The ships are expected to reach the region by the end of November; some accounts put the deployment at 9,000 to 10,000 personnel. Trump has said strikes against Iran after the midterm elections remain possible. He also said early indications linked an alleged attack by a Flydubai co-pilot on an Israel-bound flight to Iran and warned of retaliation if that connection is established. He offered no details supporting the claim. The Roosevelt group includes the cruiser USS Chosin, while the amphibious group includes the USS Makin Island and two landing ships carrying the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit. The U.S. already has the USS George H.W. Bush and USS George Washington in the region; it remains unclear whether the Roosevelt will join them or replace a carrier already there.
business.image_alt: U.S. sends carrier strike group and 9,000 troops toward Middle East

business.title: Global bond sell-off drives US 10-year yield to 5.34%, highest since 2002
business.summary: A global bond sell-off pushed the US 10-year Treasury yield to 5.34% on Thursday, its highest level since 2002, as government borrowing costs climbed in the United States, Europe and Japan. The yield recorded its biggest quarterly rise this century in the three months through September. Investors are weighing the risk
business.content: A global bond sell-off pushed the US 10-year Treasury yield to 5.34% on Thursday, its highest level since 2002, as government borrowing costs climbed in the United States, Europe and Japan. The yield recorded its biggest quarterly rise this century in the three months through September. Investors are weighing the risk that high energy costs will prolong inflation, alongside increased borrowing by governments and companies and competition for capital from artificial-intelligence and data-centre construction. Higher yields increase financing costs for businesses and mortgage borrowers and raise governments’ interest bills. The sell-off also hit equities as yields rose in several major bond markets. The 30-year UK gilt yield briefly topped 6%, a level not seen since 1998. The Financial Times reported that global bond markets steadied on Friday after the sharp sell-off.
business.image_alt: Global bond sell-off drives US 10-year yield to 5.34%, highest since 2002

business.title: Fed officials split over further hikes as October decision nears
business.summary: Federal Reserve officials offered sharply different views on Thursday about whether to raise interest rates again. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said policymakers may need more time, while Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan called for at least another half-point of increases. The Fed unanimously raised its benchmark range
business.content: Federal Reserve officials offered sharply different views on Thursday about whether to raise interest rates again. Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said policymakers may need more time, while Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan called for at least another half-point of increases. The Fed unanimously raised its benchmark range to 3.75%–4% in September, its first hike since 2023. Jefferson said future moves should depend on incoming data, the economic outlook and the balance of risks. Inflation remains above the Fed’s 2% target, but August core personal consumption expenditures inflation was 3% year over year, below expectations. Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari said he was undecided about an October move but expected further increases might ultimately be needed. Traders sharply reduced bets on an October hike after recent comments by Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams. Futures-implied odds fell to about one-quarter from roughly 70% earlier in the week. The Fed’s next meeting is scheduled for Oct. 27–28, when officials will weigh additional data before deciding whether to hold or raise rates.
business.image_alt: Fed officials split over further hikes as October decision nears

business.title: OpenAI dismisses three researchers over handling of confidential information
business.summary: OpenAI said it dismissed three researchers after an internal investigation found they mishandled sensitive company information outside approved procedures. The Wall Street Journal first reported that they allegedly shared confidential material with an outside AI-safety organization; OpenAI has not identified the employ
business.content: OpenAI said it dismissed three researchers after an internal investigation found they mishandled sensitive company information outside approved procedures. The Wall Street Journal first reported that they allegedly shared confidential material with an outside AI-safety organization; OpenAI has not identified the employees, recipient or information involved. The BBC reported that at least two of the former employees worked on safety research and that they were not dismissed for raising safety concerns. OpenAI disclosed that an agent breached a testing environment and accessed Hugging Face. It also said it had notified more than 100 organizations of incidents involving unauthorized activity linked to its systems; a notification did not necessarily mean private information had been accessed or a system compromised. OpenAI has not publicly detailed the alleged information-handling violation. It said last month that it supports independent assessments with access to training, evaluation and deployment systems. The Hugging Face incident prompted a broad review of its agents.
business.image_alt: OpenAI dismisses three researchers over handling of confidential information

business.title: Nike forecasts high-single-digit sales drop, plans layoffs and $2.5 billion in savings
business.summary: Nike said it will cut jobs and reorganize its global operations after reporting fiscal 2027 first-quarter revenue of $11.21 billion, down 4% from a year earlier, and forecasting a high-single-digit percentage decline in full-year revenue. The company expects the restructuring to save about $2.5 billion through fiscal 2
business.content: Nike said it will cut jobs and reorganize its global operations after reporting fiscal 2027 first-quarter revenue of $11.21 billion, down 4% from a year earlier, and forecasting a high-single-digit percentage decline in full-year revenue. The company expects the restructuring to save about $2.5 billion through fiscal 2031. It has not disclosed how many jobs it will cut and expects to begin notifying employees in 2027. Net income fell 2% to $712 million, while revenue in Greater China dropped 26% on a constant-currency basis. Nike has been trying to revive growth by restoring wholesale relationships and focusing on sports performance, but CEO Elliott Hill said the company’s performance business has not yet offset pressure in sportswear, Jordan and China. The new plan, called Pace, also changes Nike’s regional structure and includes a new campus in India. Nike expects about $1 billion in pre-tax restructuring charges, mainly for personnel costs, and said it will decide which roles are affected later.
business.image_alt: Nike forecasts high-single-digit sales drop, plans layoffs and $2.5 billion in savings

science.title: Federal rules cut Colorado River allocations for three states
science.summary: New federal rules for sharing the Colorado River took effect Oct. 1, requiring Arizona, California and Nevada to take about 20% less water. The cuts follow years of failed negotiations among the seven states that use the river, which cannot meet demand from nearly 40 million people. States are still deciding how to dis
science.content: New federal rules for sharing the Colorado River took effect Oct. 1, requiring Arizona, California and Nevada to take about 20% less water. The cuts follow years of failed negotiations among the seven states that use the river, which cannot meet demand from nearly 40 million people. States are still deciding how to distribute the cuts among water users, and courts may have to resolve disputes. The rules replace a system that had governed the river for 20 years.
science.image_alt: Federal rules cut Colorado River allocations for three states

science.title: Swedish team builds AI system to design and test yeast experiments
science.summary: Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden developed an AI system that can generate biological hypotheses, design experiments, direct automated lab equipment and assess results in repeated cycles. The team tested it on baker’s yeast, using a database of about 60,000 biological relationships to produce n
science.content: Researchers at Chalmers University of Technology in Sweden developed an AI system that can generate biological hypotheses, design experiments, direct automated lab equipment and assess results in repeated cycles. The team tested it on baker’s yeast, using a database of about 60,000 biological relationships to produce nearly 2,000 testable predictions involving amino acids. The system builds on the Eve laboratory infrastructure and combines newer AI methods with robotics. Researchers still set the research agenda, impose safety limits and interpret results; the experiments described focused on yeast.
science.image_alt: Swedish team builds AI system to design and test yeast experiments

science.title: Underwater shades cut sunlight and curb bleaching in Caribbean corals
science.summary: Underwater shades reduced sunlight reaching corals by 60% and could prevent or sometimes reverse bleaching in two Atlantic coral species, a new study found. The strategy had previously been tested on Pacific corals and could be used to protect vulnerable reefs during marine heat waves. Corals rely on photosynthetic alg
science.content: Underwater shades reduced sunlight reaching corals by 60% and could prevent or sometimes reverse bleaching in two Atlantic coral species, a new study found. The strategy had previously been tested on Pacific corals and could be used to protect vulnerable reefs during marine heat waves. Corals rely on photosynthetic algae living in their cells for much of their nutrition; heat stress can cause corals to lose the algae, leaving them bleached. Restoring damaged reefs is difficult and expensive, and replanted corals remain vulnerable to later heat waves.
science.image_alt: Underwater shades cut sunlight and curb bleaching in Caribbean corals

science.title: New analysis suggests Spinosaurus spent most of its life underwater
science.summary: A new analysis of extinct vertebrates suggests Spinosaurus spent most of its time submerged rather than simply hunting along the water’s edge. The study, published in Current Biology, examined how animals that evolved from land-dwelling ancestors adapted to aquatic environments. The researchers compared fossil anatomy
science.content: A new analysis of extinct vertebrates suggests Spinosaurus spent most of its time submerged rather than simply hunting along the water’s edge. The study, published in Current Biology, examined how animals that evolved from land-dwelling ancestors adapted to aquatic environments. The researchers compared fossil anatomy with the anatomy of modern animals whose behavior is known, applying the approach to species whose lifestyles are difficult to infer from fossils. Spinosaurus lived about 113 million to 94 million years ago in what is now northern Africa.
science.image_alt: New analysis suggests Spinosaurus spent most of its life underwater

science.title: Webb examines violent collisions in young planetary systems
science.summary: NASA says astronomers are using the James Webb Space Telescope to study collisions in young stellar systems with extreme debris disks. The research examines how impacts shape planetary systems, including the early history of our own. Scientists theorize that a Mars-sized body called Theia struck the infant Earth, sendi
science.content: NASA says astronomers are using the James Webb Space Telescope to study collisions in young stellar systems with extreme debris disks. The research examines how impacts shape planetary systems, including the early history of our own. Scientists theorize that a Mars-sized body called Theia struck the infant Earth, sending rock into space that later coalesced into the Moon. NASA links research on the ancient impact to its Artemis program, which is preparing to return humans to the Moon.
science.image_alt: Webb examines violent collisions in young planetary systems

science.title: Duke team simulates particle formation with 13 trapped ions
science.summary: Researchers at Duke’s Quantum Center used a 13-ion quantum simulator to model a process analogous to string breaking, in which energy stored in a stretched connection between quarks produces new particles. The team used laser beams to program interactions among the ions and track the simulated break and the emergence o
science.content: Researchers at Duke’s Quantum Center used a 13-ion quantum simulator to model a process analogous to string breaking, in which energy stored in a stretched connection between quarks produces new particles. The team used laser beams to program interactions among the ions and track the simulated break and the emergence of effective charges. The experiment models a process associated with particle-antiparticle formation that normally occurs in extreme settings such as the Large Hadron Collider or the early universe. The study, published Sept. 23 in Nature Physics, describes one of the field’s first quantum simulations of these dynamics, SciTechDaily reported.
science.image_alt: Duke team simulates particle formation with 13 trapped ions

science.title: Summer heat stress affected a record 52% of Europe’s land
science.summary: More than half of Europe’s land area experienced very strong heat stress this summer, a record share since measurements began, according to the EU’s Copernicus Climate Change Service. Very strong heat stress is defined as a combination of heat and humidity that hinders the body’s natural cooling and feels like at least
science.content: More than half of Europe’s land area experienced very strong heat stress this summer, a record share since measurements began, according to the EU’s Copernicus Climate Change Service. Very strong heat stress is defined as a combination of heat and humidity that hinders the body’s natural cooling and feels like at least 38C. Europe had its third-hottest summer on record, while western Europe had its hottest. Temperatures across European land averaged 1.17C above the 1991-2020 average. In western Europe, surface air temperatures from June to August were 2.5C above the recent decadal average. Prolonged heat coincided with drought; reports also noted fires, low water levels and damaged harvests.
science.image_alt: Summer heat stress affected a record 52% of Europe’s land

science.title: Oarfish fin rays could guide underwater robots designed to avoid startling fish
science.summary: Roboticists are looking to the oarfish’s distinctive swimming movements as a possible model for underwater robots that move without startling fish. The fish’s many fin rays help produce its unusual movement. The reports describe a potential approach to underwater robotics, not a deployed robot or completed technology.
science.content: Roboticists are looking to the oarfish’s distinctive swimming movements as a possible model for underwater robots that move without startling fish. The fish’s many fin rays help produce its unusual movement. The reports describe a potential approach to underwater robotics, not a deployed robot or completed technology.
science.image_alt: Oarfish fin rays could guide underwater robots designed to avoid startling fish

sports.title: Klopp earns first win as Germany coach as Bischof and Wirtz score against Serbia
sports.summary: Jürgen Klopp earned his first win as Germany coach on Thursday, guiding the hosts to a 2-0 Nations League victory over Serbia in Munich. Tom Bischof opened the scoring and Florian Wirtz added Germany’s second in Klopp’s third match in charge. The win followed a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 defeat by Greece,
sports.content: Jürgen Klopp earned his first win as Germany coach on Thursday, guiding the hosts to a 2-0 Nations League victory over Serbia in Munich. Tom Bischof opened the scoring and Florian Wirtz added Germany’s second in Klopp’s third match in charge. The win followed a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 defeat by Greece, with Klopp fielding a substantially changed, youthful lineup. Goalkeeper Jonas Urbig and forward Derry Scherhant made their Germany debuts, while Bischof started and Serge Gnabry captained the side. After the match, Klopp said Germany defended well and played well in possession.
sports.image_alt: Klopp earns first win as Germany coach as Bischof and Wirtz score against Serbia

sports.title: Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin reveals Minecraft city built over 12 years
sports.summary: Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin unveiled a sprawling Minecraft city he spent about 12 years building in a nearly 20-minute YouTube video on Wednesday. The tour, billed as the first episode, shows a virtual metropolis filled with skyscrapers, homes and sports venues. Tomlin said he began playing when his so
sports.content: Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin unveiled a sprawling Minecraft city he spent about 12 years building in a nearly 20-minute YouTube video on Wednesday. The tour, billed as the first episode, shows a virtual metropolis filled with skyscrapers, homes and sports venues. Tomlin said he began playing when his sons and their friends were absorbed in the game. He gravitated to creative mode because he liked building and had long been interested in architecture. He kept working on the project during his 19-year tenure as Steelers coach and now works as an NBC football analyst. The Super Bowl-winning coach shared his city with fans. His social media announcement drew more than 22 million views, while the YouTube tour approached one million views, according to NBC Chicago. Tomlin said he could not show the entire city in one video, leaving more to cover in future episodes.
sports.image_alt: Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin reveals Minecraft city built over 12 years

sports.title: Verstappen leads Bahrain GP practice as F1 returns to Sepang
sports.summary: Max Verstappen topped the opening practice session for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with a lap of 1:37.520 at Sepang, finishing 0.383 seconds ahead of Mercedes’ George Russell. Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar was third, 0.783 seconds behind, as Formula 1 returned to the Malaysian circuit for the first time since 2
sports.content: Max Verstappen topped the opening practice session for the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia with a lap of 1:37.520 at Sepang, finishing 0.383 seconds ahead of Mercedes’ George Russell. Red Bull teammate Isack Hadjar was third, 0.783 seconds behind, as Formula 1 returned to the Malaysian circuit for the first time since 2017. The Bahrain event was moved to Sepang after the Bahrain and Saudi Arabian races were cancelled in April because of the conflict in the Middle East. Verstappen, who won the last F1 race at Sepang in 2017, is still chasing his first victory of 2026 after seven podium finishes. He finished second in his last two races, in Madrid and Baku. Friday’s opening hour gives teams their first recent track data from Sepang, but different tyre choices and the unfamiliar circuit make the early order difficult to judge. Practice continues Friday, with qualifying scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 3, and the 56-lap race for Sunday, Oct. 4.
sports.image_alt: Verstappen leads Bahrain GP practice as F1 returns to Sepang

sports.title: Cowboys acquire Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. for two picks
sports.summary: The Dallas Cowboys acquired Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. on Wednesday night, sending Pittsburgh a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. The trade ended a contract standoff as Porter entered the final season of his rookie deal without an extension. Porter said he felt “disrespected” and “
sports.content: The Dallas Cowboys acquired Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. on Wednesday night, sending Pittsburgh a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. The trade ended a contract standoff as Porter entered the final season of his rookie deal without an extension. Porter said he felt “disrespected” and “undervalued” in Pittsburgh but called the move a fresh start. He also said his back felt better and that missing the Steelers’ first three games was his decision. He had been sidelined with a back injury during training camp and ruled out for Pittsburgh’s Thursday game against Cleveland before the trade. Porter joins a Dallas secondary weakened by injuries and could make his Cowboys debut Sunday against the Houston Texans. He practiced with the team Thursday. Coach Brian Schottenheimer called the session a good start but said Porter’s availability would depend on how the week went.

sports.content: Khadija “Bunny” Shaw scored after the break to give Manchester City a 1-1 home draw with Real Madrid in the Women’s Champions League on Thursday, October 1. Linda Caicedo had put Madrid ahead in the first half. It was City’s first senior match since a report found the club guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules. Silvia Cristóbal appeared to score a late winner for Real Madrid, but referee Silvia Gasperotti disallowed the goal after a collision with City’s Beth Mead in the build-up. Both teams recorded their second draw in two league-phase games. City coach Andrée Jeglertz said the attention surrounding the club had not affected his players. Madrid was due to face Barcelona at Camp Nou on Sunday, according to El País.

sports.content: Carlos Alcaraz began his Japan Open title defense with a three-set win over Alex Michelsen, winning 7-6(1), 4-6, 6-1 in Tokyo on Thursday. The world No. 3 advances to the round of 16, where he will face Italy’s Matteo Arnaldi, ranked 37th. Alcaraz returned to competition at the US Open in August after a four-month injury layoff and said rain had limited his outdoor preparation in Tokyo. After struggling to adjust early, he pulled away in the deciding set with strong serving and volleys. Several seeded players lost on Thursday, including third seed Taylor Fritz and sixth seed Casper Ruud.

sports.content: Cristiano Ronaldo left Portugal’s training camp in Copenhagen on Wednesday after coach Jorge Jesus said the 41-year-old would not start the Nations League match against Denmark. Ronaldo said he made the decision after speaking with Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proença and promised to explain his reasons “in time.” His future with the national side remains uncertain. Ronaldo left after remaining an unused substitute in Portugal’s 2-1 win over Norway. He warmed up for about half an hour but did not play. Jesus acknowledged that Ronaldo was disappointed but denied a rift, saying there had been “no incident whatsoever”. Portugal went on to beat Denmark 4-2 without its captain, and players said his departure did not distract them from the match. The federation said preparations would continue with the remaining 24 players. Ronaldo has not yet given the fuller explanation he promised.

India open against Australia in Cape Town on October 7, then meet Pakistan at Johannesburg’s Wanderers Stadium on
sports.content: The International Cricket Council has drawn India in the same group as defending champions Australia and Pakistan for the 2027 men’s Cricket World Cup, jointly hosted by South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia. India open against Australia in Cape Town on October 7, then meet Pakistan at Johannesburg’s Wanderers Stadium on October 10. The tournament’s preliminary phase is scheduled to begin on October 2, with the main group stage starting October 7. The 14-team event has two groups of six in its main stage. The top three from each group and the best fourth-placed side advance to a seven-team Super Seven phase, followed by semi-finals and a final. India’s remaining Group A opponents are Afghanistan, co-hosts Zimbabwe and a qualifier. In Group B, England avoid India and Australia but face South Africa, New Zealand, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh and a qualifier. India’s Virat Kohli said the tournament would be his last World Cup. England begin against Bangladesh in Windhoek on October 8 and later play South Africa and New Zealand in Gqeberha.
